Fixture: 64_vardct_lfgroupseam_rgb_128x2176_nofilters_d6.jxl
128x2176 RGB, VarDCT lossy, gaborish and EPF disabled, d=6.0, effort 3

Purpose
-------
The first fixture in this tree with more than one **LF group**. LF groups are
2048x2048 samples, so every other fixture here is a single LF group and no
test could see what happens at an internal LF-group boundary. This one is
2176 rows tall: one horizontal seam, at y = 2048.

It currently FAILS, on purpose, and its rung in
crates/jpxl-decode/tests/e2e_vardct.rs is #[ignore]d with the diagnosis. The
whole error budget is at the seam:

    peak 0.010567  (X 0.010567, Y 0.002333, B 0.008631)
    peak outside rows 2030..2066: 3.3e-6

That is the signature of I.5.2's adaptive LF smoothing being applied per LF
group instead of over the frame-wide LF image: JPXL leaves the first and last
row and column of each LF group's own plane unsmoothed, but I.5.2 says the
pass runs for each LF sample "of the image" that is not in the first or last
row or column -- so only the frame's own edges are excluded and an internal
seam must be smoothed across, using the neighbouring LF group's samples. The
band is 16 rows (the two 8x8 block rows either side of the seam), which is
exactly what an unsmoothed LF block row expands to through I.8/I.9.

The same defect is what keeps the `bike` / `bike_5` conformance rungs red;
this fixture reproduces it without needing the corpus fetched. See
docs/experiments/2026-08-04-negative-transfer-function-branch.md section 6.

Why these encoder settings
--------------------------
-d 6.0 -e 3 is load-bearing. At -d 1.0 cjxl sets kSkipAdaptiveLFSmoothing and
the seam vanishes entirely (measured: peak 3e-6 over the whole image). The
smoothing pass has to actually run for this fixture to prove anything.

--gaborish=0 --epf=0 disables both restoration filters, so the seam is not
smeared by Annex J and the band's extent is exactly the LF block rows. Per
18181-3 Annex A Table A.1:

    Part 3 error class:  peak <= 0.004,  RMSE <= 1e-5   (no filters)

Provenance
----------
  Encoder:      cjxl v0.13.0 196a43d9 [_AVX2_,SSE4,SSE2] {GNU 15.2.0}
  libjxl rev:   196a43d996aa6ed33ebf98812a7c6d43b2b6d01b (v0.12-snapshot-2-g196a43d9)
  cjxl flags:   -d 6.0 --gaborish=0 --epf=0 -e 3
  Built by:     tools/setup-oracles.sh (flags recorded in
                tools/oracle-bin/PINNED_REVISIONS.txt)
  Regenerate:   tools/make-vardct-fixtures.sh
                That script IS the recipe; it rewrites the source and re-encodes.

  Source image: tests/fixtures/generated/src_vardct_lfgroupseam_rgb_128x2176.ppm  (835600 bytes)
                sha256 1307e39ef19f9dd5e5933a6208dba4d42df357a18af9356275d07e075d2367ad
                Pixel formula, integer arithmetic only (so it is byte-identical
                on any platform), with tri(t, p) the triangle wave
                0 .. p/2 .. 0 over one period p:
                  channel c = (24 + 2*tri(2x + y + 11c, 150)
                                  + tri(y, 96) + 2*tri(5x + c, 32)) & 0xFF
                Piecewise linear, hence locally smooth, which is what makes
                I.5.2's max(0, 3 - 4*gap) factor non-zero and the smoothing
                pass actually change samples.

  Fixture:      11474 bytes
                sha256 16a1ade870348c108ced7fc302eda291b222e7bf5634e23804be7fefc623e03b

  Reference decode (djxl --output_format npy): NOT committed -- 3342417 bytes,
  far over this repo's 100 KB commit-next-to-fixture cutoff (see
  tools/make-vardct-fixtures.sh). Regenerate with:
    tools/oracle-bin/djxl --output_format npy \
      tests/fixtures/handmade/64_vardct_lfgroupseam_rgb_128x2176_nofilters_d6.jxl \
      /tmp/64.npy
  sha256 (pinned decoder, tools/oracle-bin/PINNED_REVISIONS.txt):
    3546e42f47cc647d211e9a9a3674fcfe7bdb77139ca1de9e8c2b030df553c954
  Shape (1, 2176, 128, 3) little-endian f32, per 18181-3 4.1.2. Decode is
  deterministic per libjxl revision, so this hash is expected to reproduce
  exactly on the pinned oracle build.

cjxl/djxl are used strictly as BLACK BOXES: they emit/consume conformant
streams for JPXL to parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a
different libjxl revision changes these digests, that is the point of
recording them -- do not silently update them; note the revision change.
